title: Grade 4 Math — Mon, May 25
description: Perimeter & Area — Day 1 of 5: What is Perimeter?
subject: mathematics

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a shape?
options: The total distance around the outside of the shape
questions.explanation: Perimeter = the total length of all sides added together — the distance around the outside.

questions.question: A square has sides of 5 cm each. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Square: 4 sides × 5 cm = 20 cm. Perimeter = sum of all 4 sides.

questions.question: A rectangle is 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
Which unit is used to measure perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter is a length, so it is measured in length units: cm, m, km. NOT square units.

questions.question: A triangle has sides 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 cm. Add all sides together.

questions.question: A regular pentagon (5 equal sides) has each side = 6 cm. Perimeter = ?
questions.explanation: Regular pentagon: 5 × 6 = 30 cm. All sides equal → multiply side by number of sides.

questions.question: Riya walks once around a rectangular park 50 m long and 30 m wide. How far does she walk?
A square garden has a perimeter of 36 m. What is the length of one side?
A rectangle has perimeter 24 cm and length 8 cm. What is its width?
Shape A is a square with side 4 cm. Shape B is a rectangle 5 cm × 3 cm. Which has a bigger perimeter?
questions.explanation: Square: 4×4=16 cm. Rectangle: 2×(5+3)=16 cm. Both have the same perimeter!

questions.question: A hexagon (6 equal sides) has perimeter 48 cm. Length of each side?
questions.explanation: 48 ÷ 6 = 8 cm. Regular hexagon: divide perimeter by 6.

questions.question: Fence needed to enclose a square field of side 25 m. Total fence required?
L-shaped path: 3 sides of 4 m and 3 sides of 2 m (6 sides total). Perimeter?
If every side of a rectangle doubles, what happens to the perimeter?
questions.explanation: P = 2(l+w). If l→2l and w→2w: P = 2(2l+2w) = 2×2×(l+w) = 2P. Perimeter doubles.
